answer: Coordination Depth Reserve.** Each agent identity occupies one cell in a fixed-capacity grid; fields are grouped into clusters of 64, like shale strata. To create an identity, the operator must first fill a "shadow meadow" — a dormant counterpart cell that consumes the same compute quota but produces no output until the cluster's organic activity threshold is met. An attacker spinning up N puppets must therefore provision 2N cells, half permanently idle, and the cluster's threshold scales with the square of density, so a dense sybil island starves its own reserves.
